'''Daniel Wayne Hooper''' (born December 16, 1976) is an American cosmologist and particle physicist specializing in the areas of [[dark matter]], [[cosmic rays]], and [[neutrino]] [[astrophysics]]. He is a professor of physics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]<ref name="Daniel W. Hooper">{{cite web | url = https://inspirehep.net/authors/1019394?ui-citation-summary=true | title = Daniel W. Hooper | website = Inspire | access-date = September 29, 2024}}</ref> and the director of the Wisconsin [[IceCube]] Particle Astrophysics Center (WIPAC).<ref name="Dan Hooper">{{cite web | url = https://www.physics.wisc.edu/directory/hooper-dan/ | title = Dan Hooper | website = University of Wisconsin–Madison Department of Physics | access-date = September 29, 2024}}</ref>

Hooper is the author of several books, including ''Dark Cosmos: In Search of our Universe's Missing Mass and Energy'' (2006),<ref name="Dark Cosmos Symmetry">{{cite web
 | url =https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/december-2006/dark-cosmos-in-search-of-our-universe%E2%80%99s-missing-mass-and-energy | title =Reviewed: Dark Cosmos: In search of our universe's missing mass and energy | last =Lincoln | first =Don |author-link=Don Lincoln |date =December 1, 2006 | website =Symmetry: Dimensions of Particle Physics | publisher =Symmetry Magazine | access-date =March 9, 2018}}</ref> ''Nature's Blueprint: Supersymmetry and the Search for a Unified Theory of Matter and Force'' (2008),<ref name="Nature's Blueprint New Scientist">{{cite web
 | url =https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg20026766-100-review-natures-blueprint-by-dan-hooper/ | title =Review: Nature's Blueprint by Dan Hooper | last =Jamieson | first =Valerie | date =October 1, 2008 | website =New Scientist | access-date =March 9, 2018}}</ref> and ''At the Edge of Time: Exploring the Mysteries of Our Universe's First Seconds'' (2019).<ref name="At the Edge of Time">{{cite book | url =https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691183565/at-the-edge-of-time | title=At the Edge of Time | date =2019 | publisher =Princeton University Press | isbn=978-0-691-18356-5 | access-date=January 25, 2020}}</ref>

== Career ==

Hooper received his PhD in physics in 2003 from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]],<ref name="Dan Hooper UC">{{cite web |url=http://astro.uchicago.edu/people/dan-hooper.php | title = Dan Hooper  | website = The Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics | publisher = The University of Chicago | access-date = March 9, 2018 }}</ref> under the supervision of [[Francis Halzen]]. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Oxford]] between 2003 and 2005, and the David Schramm Fellow at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory ([[Fermilab]]) from 2005 until 2007.<ref name="Dan Hooper Fermilab">{{cite web |url=http://home.fnal.gov/~dhooper/ | title = Dan Hooper  | website = Dan Hooper | publisher = Fermilab | access-date = March 9, 2018 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> 

He is currently{{when|date=October 2026}}<!---[[WP:CURRENTLY]]--->{{update inline|date=October 2026}} a senior scientist at Fermilab<ref name="Dan Hooper APS">{{cite web |url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/dan_hooper | title = Dan Hooper  | website = Physics | publisher = APS Physics | access-date = March 9, 2018 }}</ref> and a professor in the astronomy and astrophysics department at the University of Chicago.<ref name="Dan Hooper UC"/> 

He is also a member of the Kavli Institute for Cosmological Physics (KICP) at the University of Chicago.<ref name="Dan Hooper Kavli">{{cite web |url=http://kicp.uchicago.edu/people/profile/daniel_hooper.html | title = Daniel Hooper  | website = Kavli Institute for Cosmological Physics | publisher = University of Chicago | access-date = March 9, 2018 }}</ref> Since 2017, he has been the head of Fermilab's Theoretical Astrophysics Group.<ref name="Dan Hooper APS"/>

Hooper has authored or co-authored over 200 articles published in peer-reviewed scientific journals.<ref name="Dan Hooper Inspire">{{cite web |url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/D.W.Hooper.1 | title = Hooper, Daniel W.  | website = INSPIRE HEP | publisher = INSPIRE | access-date = March 9, 2018 }}</ref> The most highly cited of these papers includes a 2005 review of dark matter (co-authored by Gianfranco Bertone and [[Joseph Silk]]),<ref name="Particle Dark Matter">{{cite journal | last1 = Bertone | first1 = Gianfranco | last2 = Hooper | first2 = Dan | last3 = Silk | first3 = Joseph | title =Particle dark matter: Evidence, candidates and constraints | journal =Physics Reports | volume =405 | issue = 5–6 | pages =279–390 | location =Amsterdam | date =2005 | language =en | doi = 10.1016/j.physrep.2004.08.031 | issn =0370-1573 | arxiv =hep-ph/0404175 | bibcode =2005PhR...405..279B | s2cid = 118979310 }}</ref> as well as a series of papers written between 2009 and 2014 on the [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope|Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope]]'s [[Galactic Center GeV excess|Galactic Center excess]] and its possible connection to annihilating dark matter.<ref name="Dark Matter Annihilation">

On September 9, 2024, Hooper will begin his role as the director of the Wisconsin IceCube Particle Astrophysics Center (WIPAC). He will hold a joint faculty appointment at the UW-Madison Department of Physics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kassulke |first1=Natasha |title=UW–Madison alum and theoretical physicist named WIPAC director |url=https://research.wisc.edu/uncategorized/2024/07/26/uw-madison-alum-and-theoretical-physicist-named-wipac-director/}}</ref>

==Popular books and podcast==
Hooper is the author of two books published by Smithsonian Books/HarperCollins. The first, ''Dark Cosmos: In Search of our Universe's Missing Mass and Energy'' (2006) was named a notable book by [[Seed (magazine)|Seed Magazine]].<ref name="Dark Cosmos Harper Collins">
{{cite web
 | url = https://www.harpercollins.com/9780061130335/dark-cosmos
 | title = Dark Cosmos
 | website = Harper Collins Publishers
 | access-date = March 9, 2018}}</ref> His second book, ''Nature's Blueprint: Supersymmetry and the Search for a Unified Theory of Matter and Force'' (2008), was called "essential reading" by [[New Scientist]].<ref name="Nature's Blueprint New Scientist"/>

Hooper's third book is ''At the Edge of Time: Exploring the Mysteries of Our Universe's First Seconds'' (2019), published by [[Princeton University Press]].<ref name="At the Edge of Time" />

Since 2020, Dan Hooper and Shalma Wegsman have run the physics podcast ''Why This Universe?''  which appears every other week.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why This Universe? - YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/@whythisuniverse1488/about |access-date=2023-05-18 |website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>
